newsitem.title: JAPAN: Honda mulls revising down output plan for July.
newsitem.headline: Honda mulls revising down output plan for July.

text.p: Honda Motor Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it was considering lowering its production plan for July.

"We are considering whether or not we should adjust our production plan for July as we have found that reaction to the boost in demand ahead of the consumption tax increase was larger than expected," a Honda spokesman said.
Japan raised it consumption tax on April 1 to five percent from three percent.
"We are planning to operate four of our five production lines for two extra days in July, but we are now wondering if we will really need to do so," the spokesman said.
The business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Wednesday that Honda would cut its domestic output of recreational vehicles by several thousand units from July in light of the drop in demand.
The spokesman said the company had not made a decision yet.
Sales of Honda cars, excluding minicars, have fallen since April, and were down 15 percent year-on-year in May, the paper said.
It said that Honda's current monthly output was 90,000 units, but the company spokesman said the figure did not include output of minicars.
